messages.subject: Explicit integration with RMHMC
parts:
I thought some people here might be interested in this:

http://arxiv.org/abs/1211.3759

Girolami and others have come up with a way to perform Riemann Manifold HMC with an explicit integration method, making it much more efficient.  I haven't gone through it in detail yet, but it looks very promising and the trick they use to do it is very simple but fairly clever, ie, changing from Hamiltonian dynamics to Lagrangian dynamics.

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Explicit integration with RMHMC
parts:
Marcus

Yup, I brought that to the attention of the local Stan group as soon as it came out.  Unfortunately there are some subtleties to their method - they not only transform to a Lagrangian perspective but also make some approximations to the resulting integrator.  This kills the symplectness (and hence long term stability) of the integrator -and- degrades the error from eps^2 to eps.  They even admit that the new integrator is only advantageous in low dimensions (see their experiments section) where RMHMC wouldn't be necessary anyways.  But the integrator is a serious issue in RMHMC and we're definitely paying attention!

-Mike
